title: The Fourth Possibility
next_chapter_hook: Mo Xiansheng's lingering voice echoes again: The time has come, the final face of the Imperial Tomb. The death prophecy of Chapter Seven Hundred is about to be revealed, the ultimate solution approaches.

text.content: "A signal completely matching your genetic profile has been detected within the dimensional rift!" The alarm from the Celestial Eye exploded like thunder, and Chen Ji's fingers gripping the Tianji Record Fragment tightened abruptly. Genetic match—these four words crashed like monstrous waves in his mind. His sister, lost for seven years—Chen Nian, taken by the Holy Sect to serve as the Heavenly Fate Lock Key. The sole existence capable of disrupting the Tianji Record's foresight was now, at the other end of the dimensional rift, releasing a bloodline's call. Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly pressing the surging emotions into the deepest corners of his heart. He understood that now was not the time for sentimentality. The Celestial Eye's observational data, the Turtle Shell coordinate anchor point, the power of fate inscription, Su Qingyao's blood resonance—all these fragments were spinning madly within his mind, awaiting to be pieced into a complete map.

The Tianji Record Fragment glowed with a ghostly blue light in Chen Ji's palm, while Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul phantom faintly emerged on the page. "Do you sense it?" Mo Xiansheng's voice was hoarse and weary. "That is the signal of the Heavenly Fate Lock Key. Her existence itself interferes with the Tianji Record—any foresight involving her appears blurred. Yet conversely, she might be the key to breaking the Tianji Record's shackles." Chen Ji remained silent, simply closing his eyes. In the darkness, four paths he had deduced countless times re-emerged: replacing Heavenly Dao, becoming a new Chess Player, mutually destroying with Heavenly Dao, or limply surviving within Heavenly Dao's chess game. Each path was a dead end, or at least a dead end in Mo Xiansheng's perspective. Yet now, a fifth path emerged—blurred, uncertain, demanding his utmost effort to deduce. Yet it existed within possibility.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji, your hand is trembling. Su Qingyao had silently approached his side, her gaze falling upon the faintly glowing fragment, a flicker of heartache passing through her eyes. As the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, she had witnessed countless times Chen Ji's composed demeanor of flawless calculation, yet this was the first she observed him so unsettled. "Blood resonance... I can help you locate the source of that signal." She proactively extended her hand, a faint golden pattern emerging in her palm. "Using my blood as a guide, perhaps you can see more clearly." Chen Ji abruptly opened his eyes, a complex emotion flickering in his gaze as he looked at Su Qingyao. This woman, thrice approaching the truth yet thrice being resolved by him, now without hesitation entrusted her bloodline power to him. "...Alright." He uttered only a single word, yet it carried countless unspoken words.

text.content: Su Qingyao's bloodline power wound around Chen Ji's perception like golden threads, the signal from the dimensional rift instantly becoming clear. Chen Ji's consciousness seemed to traverse an endless void, touching a blurred yet real coordinate—there was Chen Nian's aura, weakly yet stubbornly pulsating, like a candle flame about to extinguish in the wind. Simultaneously, the Celestial Eye's massive observational data flooded his mind like a tide. The operational patterns of the Three Realms' Heavenly Dao, the fate trajectories of past predictors, every trace the Tianji Record left in the river of time—all information collided, intertwined, and reorganized in his mind. The Turtle Shell coordinate anchor point began to spin madly, fragments of the fate inscription power embedding one by one into his mental framework. Countless light points reflected in Chen Ji's pupils—those were the fate threads of three thousand worlds, weaving before his eyes into an unprecedented net.

Not replacement, not mutual destruction, not limply surviving. A smile suddenly curved the corners of Chen Ji's lips, carrying a hint of madness yet also a sense of liberation. Mo Xiansheng had said that the Tianji Record was Heavenly Dao's chess piece, and the Eye of Heavenly Dao used predictors as tools. Generations of predictors had all contemplated how to defeat Heavenly Dao, how to replace Heavenly Dao, how to coexist with Heavenly Dao—yet they had never posed the most fundamental question: Why must there be a 'Heavenly Dao'? Why must there be a 'Chess Player'? Chen Ji's thinking broke through its shackles at this moment. He saw the fifth path—not the counterattack of a chess piece, not the compromise of a chess piece, but utterly shattering the chessboard. Let all chess pieces become observers, let the trajectory of fate be collectively inscribed by all beings, rather than determined by a transcendent consciousness.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes and transmitted a message through blood resonance to Chen Nian on the other side of the dimensional rift: Sister, I found the way, wait for me.

Three entry paths formed a complete strategic map in Chen Ji's mind, but he knew the true key was not in choosing which path—but in merging all three into one. The Heavenly Secrets Core was the target, the Turtle Shell anchor was the medium, and blood resonance was the foundation. None could be dispensed with. He silently deduced in his heart: if only rewriting the Heavenly Secrets Core without anchor diffusion, the rule seed would be easily cleared by the Eye of Heavenly Secrets; if only anchor diffusion without blood resonance as foundation, sentient beings could not truly comprehend and use observational abilities; if only blood awakening without rewriting the Heavenly Secrets Core, sentient beings would forever struggle within predetermined rules. A gleam flashed in Chen Ji's eyes. Perfect.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji, what do you see? Su Qingyao's voice pulled Chen Ji back from his deduction. She stood beside him, golden bloodline markings slowly fading, but her gaze remained firmly locked on Chen Ji's eyes. In those eyes she could never quite penetrate, she saw something for the first time she could comprehend—a light that only appears in a long-separated sister hearing her brother's voice. "I see a path," Chen Ji's voice was low but firm. "A path Master Mo never imagined, that no prophet throughout the ages has ever walked. Not defeating the Heavenly Dao, not replacing the Heavenly Dao, not mutual destruction with the Heavenly Dao—but making the Heavenly Dao no longer necessary." Su Qingyao froze. "Making the Heavenly Dao... no longer necessary?"

text.content: Chen Ji turned to face the three-realm sand table projected by the Heavenly Eye, his voice like a bell pronouncing destiny. "Why does the Eye of Heavenly Secrets seek to become a chess player? Because sentient beings require order, need foresight, demand a transcendent existence to arrange fate. Yet this very need constitutes the foundation of Heavenly Secrets' existence." He extended his hand, pointing to the luminous point at the sand table's center representing Heavenly Secrets' will. "The core of the fourth possibility is to make sentient beings their own observers. Each grain of sand possesses the capacity to perceive destiny, each breeze can touch the river of time. Then the Eye of Heavenly Secrets would cease to be an indispensable chess player, becoming merely one among numerous observers—perhaps even the most ordinary." He turned to look at Su Qingyao, his eyes burning with unprecedented intensity. "What we must accomplish is not to defeat it, but to render it insignificant."

text.content: Chen Ji grasped Su Qingyao's hand, golden bloodline markings converging in their palms, and the blueprint of the fourth possibility surged like a tide into her consciousness.

Chen Ji's consciousness connection with the Tianji Record reached an unprecedented depth at this moment. He felt like he had transformed into a swimming fish, ascending upstream along the river of time to touch the source of the three-realm Heavenly Secrets—an existence transcending time and space. There, he witnessed the Eye of Heavenly Secrets' true form: a massive eye woven from countless threads of fate, calculating every sentient being's trajectory, the consequences of every choice, and every possible future at incomprehensible speeds. It was perfect, yet profoundly solitary. It knew everything, yet could be known by no other existence. Chen Ji extended his hand and gently placed the seed of the fourth possibility's laws at this eye's core.

The moment the law seed fell into the Heavenly Secrets Core, the entire three-realm sand table violently trembled. Golden light spread from the Eye of Heavenly Secrets' center in all directions, and wherever it passed, every grain of sand began to emit faint fluorescence—the precursor of sentient beings' awakening. Chen Ji saw fragments of that future through the Tianji Record: a world without chess players, where every grain of sand possessed the ability to perceive destiny. They no longer needed the Heavenly Secrets' guidance because each choice itself was guidance. Fate was no longer a unidirectional river but countless interwoven threads, with every sentient being being a weaver. The Tianji Record violently trembled in Chen Ji's palm, and Master Mo's phantom manifested again, but this time, his expression held not worry but a certain sense of release.

dialogue.content: "You did it." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a tremor. "Throughout the ages, predictors have contemplated how to defeat, replace, or coexist—only you dared to ask the most fundamental question: why must there be a Chess Player?" His phantom began to fade, yet a smile lingered on his lips. "Your path is correct. But remember, the fourth possibility is merely a framework; the true flesh and blood must be filled in by yourself. The Heavenly Secrets' Eye will not stand idly by—it will attempt to destroy all awakened seeds before you complete your work." Chen Ji was about to speak when Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed once more, weaker this time yet carrying undeniable gravity: "The moment has arrived. Come see me one last time at the Imperial Tomb. It is time to unravel the death prophecy of the Seven Hundredth Chapter."

text.content: "Before the words faded, Mo Xiansheng's phantom dissolved completely into the air, leaving only the golden sealing pattern on the Tianji Record Fragment that had not yet fully vanished. Chen Ji stared at that pattern for a long while, until Su Qingyao softly called his name. 'Imperial Tomb...' he murmured, 'Seventh Hundredth Chapter.' That was the death prophecy left by his past life—or rather, by the previous inheritor of the Tianji Record. Mo Xiansheng had always refused to reveal its contents, merely saying 'the time is not yet right.' And now, the time had come. Across the dimensional rift, Chen Nian's aura seemed to sense something, the vague signal becoming slightly clearer, as if responding to this breakthrough."

choice.prompt: "Mo Xiansheng's summons and Chen Nian's signal appeared simultaneously—Chen Ji had to make a choice."

choices.description: "Mo Xiansheng's final guidance concerns the ultimate solution to the death prophecy in the Seventh Hundredth Chapter. Not a moment can be wasted."

dialogue.content: "Su Qingyao gripped his hand: 'I will accompany you.' Her tone brooked no argument. 'Whatever lies within the Imperial Tomb, we face it together.'"

choices.description: "Chen Nian is the key to the fourth possibility, and the signal from the dimensional rift may vanish at any moment—my sister's safety is paramount."
choices.visible_cost: "Missing Mo Xiansheng's optimal guidance timing means the death prophecy may never be unraveled."
choices.visible_reward: "Successfully rescue Chen Nian, unlock the 'Heavenly Fate Key' bloodline ability, granting the fourth possibility its strongest foundation."
choices.risk_hint: "The Imperial Tomb summons has a time limit; Mo Xiansheng may not wait for a second opportunity."

text.content: "Chen Ji closed his eyes, passing information to Chen Nian through Bloodline Resonance: Sister, wait for me a little longer. The signal from the dimensional rift's other side quivered faintly, as if responding."

"Chen Ji stood before the Heaven's Eye Sand Table, behind him the Heavenly Secrets Core he had just inscribed, before him the Void Rift leading to the Imperial Tomb, and in the distance—across the dimensional rift—his sister missing for seven years. The Tianji Record Fragment in his palm radiated gentle warmth, seemingly urging him toward a decision. The framework of the fourth possibility was complete, yet it remained merely a skeleton, requiring final filling to become a complete life. Mo Xiansheng said 'the time has arrived,' implying that the death prophecy of the Seventh Hundredth Chapter held the key answer. Chen Nian's presence was both noise disrupting the Tianji Record's Foresight and a key breaking shackles. A difficult choice lay before Chen Ji, but he knew that whichever path he chose, he had already taken the most crucial step."

dialogue.content: "Whatever you choose, I will be by your side." Su Qingyao's voice was calm and resolute, her Bloodline Power having generated a profound resonance with Chen Ji, enabling her to sense his hesitation and struggle. Chen Ji turned to look at her—this man who had approached truth three times yet chose to trust her—now revealed a rare smile. Not calculation, not pretense, but genuine, heartfelt gratitude. "Let's go," he said. "To the Imperial Tomb." Chen Nian's signal was important, but Mo Xiansheng had waited too long, and the death prophecy of the Seventh Hundredth Chapter determined the success or failure of the entire fourth possibility. He had to unravel that years-long mystery before rescuing his sister."

text.content: "The Heaven's Eye Sand Table dissolved gently. Chen Ji tucked the Tianji Record Fragment into his chest and stepped into the Void Rift leading to the Imperial Tomb alongside Su Qingyao. The moment the rift sealed, he cast one final glance toward the dimensional rift—where Chen Nian's aura remained faint yet stubbornly flickering, like an inexhaustible star. He knew his sister was waiting. And upon his return from the Imperial Tomb, he would go to retrieve her. The fourth possibility had been inscribed into the Heavenly Secrets Core, Mo Xiansheng's final guidance was about to be revealed, the Seven Hundredth Chapter's death prophecy would soon be unraveled—every endpoint seemed to beckon him. Yet Chen Ji understood clearly that the Heavenly Secrets' Eye would never stand by indifferently. Before he touched the ultimate truth, the most dangerous backlash might be just beginning."
